config.title: Dessau Day Trip from Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Trains, tickets, opening days and timing for a Bauhaus day in Dessau from Berlin.

items.q: How long does it take to get from Berlin to Dessau?
items.a: Until 20 November 2026 about **2 hours 10 minutes** from Berlin Hauptbahnhof, with the RE3 to Lutherstadt Wittenberg and the RB51 to Dessau, because the RE7 is replaced by buses between Bad Belzig and Dessau. From 21 November the RE7 runs from Berlin-Charlottenburg to Dessau in about 1 hour 30 minutes.

items.q: Is the Deutschlandticket valid for a Dessau day trip?
items.a: Yes. The **Deutschlandticket** covers the RE3, RB51 and RE7. The Quer-durchs-Land-Ticket also works on regional trains, but on weekdays only from 09:00. The Brandenburg-Berlin-Ticket does not reach Dessau, and an ICE needs a normal DB ticket.

items.q: Is the Bauhaus Dessau open on Mondays?
items.a: From March to October the Bauhaus Building and the Masters' Houses open on Mondays, but the **Bauhaus Museum Dessau is closed**. From November to February **all three sites are closed on Mondays**.

items.q: Are there guided tours in English at the Bauhaus Dessau?
items.a: Only on **Fridays from March to October**: 12:00 in the Bauhaus Building, 13:30 at the Masters' Houses and 15:30 in the museum. From November to February there are no public tours in English.

items.q: How much does it cost to visit the Bauhaus in Dessau?
items.a: The Bauhaus Building is 14 euros, the Masters' Houses and the Bauhaus Museum 10 euros each. The **all-in-one ticket at 29 euros** covers all three plus the Konsum Building and is valid for three consecutive days. Visitors aged 18 and under go free.

items.q: Can I see the Bauhaus Dessau in one day from Berlin?
items.a: Yes, if you arrive by about 10:00 and go Tuesday to Friday. Start at the Bauhaus Building, walk 10 minutes to the Masters' Houses, then cross to the museum east of the station. The 18:10 RB51 gets you back to Berlin Hauptbahnhof at 20:20.
